generation.explanation: The inscribed angle theorem says that an angle whose vertex P lies on a circle and whose sides pass through two fixed points A and B (intercepting arc AB) measures exactly half the central angle ∠AOB that subtends the same arc. So as you drag P along an arc, ∠APB stays constant — and if you cross to the other arc between A and B, it jumps to a different constant (half of the reflex arc).
